brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer at a corner of a cell
requirements.evidence: drawer:0#0,0#cut on piece:0,0,0;half-n at its cut/south face

requirements.requirement: One spike at the very same corner of the same cell
requirements.evidence: No spike socket exists at that corner: spike requires junction of three cells meeting; half-n drawer cell plus neighbours does not offer a spike at same junction as drawer. Tested all neighbours - find_sockets spike returned 0 total.

requirements.requirement: Drawer and spike touching at same corner
requirements.evidence: Cannot co-locate: configurator enforces different geometry rules - drawer sits on cut face of half base, spike needs three cells around junction. No build offers both at identical corner; attempted L-shapes and stacked cells, all refused.

finish.summary: Drawer placed on half-n base; spike cannot occupy same corner - geometry rules prohibit co-location, so requirement is unmet as configurator-enforced.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
